clue.text: Savoury dish cook won't get the bird for

definitions.meaning: a savoury of scrambled egg on toast spread with anchovy paste

definitions.text: cook won't get the bird for
definitions.meaning: to scotch is to stop or thwart, so to scotch a game bird is to stop it reaching the cook

explanation.surface: A chef is told a savoury will be served without the expected game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOTCH WOODCOCK is a British savoury, a small dish served at the end of a meal. Read as a verb phrase, to scotch the woodcock is to prevent it, so the cook never gets the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British savoury course of anchovy toast topped with creamy scrambled egg; the second reading puts the verb to thwart before the game bird.

clue.text: Striking sail?

definitions.meaning: something striking or remarkably fine is, in old slang, a spanking one, and a hitter is one who spanks
a fore-and-aft sail set on the aftermost mast of a ship

explanation.surface: A question about whether a sail could be called striking.
explanation.definitionFit: One who strikes with a smack is a spanker; the same word names a fore-and-aft sail on the mizzen mast.

clue.text: In any case he seems to be against taking, legal advice

definitions.text: In any case he seems to be against taking, legal advice

parts.words: In any case he seems to be against taking, legal advice
parts.note: in every legal case this barrister speaks for the other side, so he seems set against the advice his own side's lawyer gives

explanation.surface: Someone appears to refuse legal advice in every situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any case' means 'whatever happens' on the surface, but here it is a court case, where the lawyer for the other side opposes you.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrister acting for the other party in a lawsuit argues against you in every trial.

clue.text: Restrain youngster embracing Rex

indicators.note: the youngster's word holds the king's letter within its arms, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone holds back a child who is hugging a dog called Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: To check or hold in, as a rider does with the chain under a horse's jaw, is to keep back.

clue.text: Manage to get it from a Western point of view

parts.note: an angle is a standpoint or slant on a subject

explanation.surface: Achieving something by looking at it from a cowboy's perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something by contrivance or cunning persuasion is to manoeuvre it into your hands.

clue.text: Warm-hearted leaving the office, maybe'

definitions.meaning: friendly and sociable, at ease with other people
an official on the way out, about to give up a post

explanation.surface: A friendly colleague is about to leave the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The office' looks like a workplace, but it is a public post that someone is retiring from.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable, friendly nature is described by one word; the same word describes a holder of a post who is about to retire.

clue.text: Transitory move on the tennis court

definitions.text: Transitory move on the tennis court

parts.words: Transitory move on the tennis court
parts.note: players swap ends of the court during a tennis match, a brief move from one side to the other

explanation.surface: A fleeting movement made by a player during a game of tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the players switch ends after odd-numbered games; more generally the word means a switch from one system to another.

clue.text: Hunter always' in the pink?

parts.note: a fox-hunter rides in a pink (scarlet) coat, so a being always in this riding dress is one fixed in its habit

explanation.surface: Asks whether a hunter is forever in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' means healthy, but hunting coats are called pink; a habit is also riding dress, so a hunter always so clad is a person of fixed routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps rigidly to routines, with habit read as the riding dress a hunter always wears.

clue.text: She's familiar' with Elizabeth the st, that is

parts.note: Bess is a pet form of the name Elizabeth
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A woman known informally by a short form of Elizabeth's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a damaged stretch ('the st') that gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet form of a woman's name, the kind used by family and friends, so a familiar version.

clue.text: Distributed in pairs can be painstaking

indicators.note: letters handed out and spread around are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Something shared out two at a time turns out to require great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' rearranges IN PAIRS. 'Painstaking' looks like 'very careful', but read as pain's taking: the tablet takes the pain away.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkilling tablet, read as something that takes away pain.

clue.text: Apparatus for highly-trained fliers

parts.note: circus acrobats who swing high above the ring are both skilled and trained up high

explanation.surface: Equipment for expertly trained pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly-trained fliers' suggests elite pilots; it is acrobats trained high up under the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal bar hung on ropes, on which circus acrobats swing through the air.

clue.text: Gentle touch on the snooker table

definitions.meaning: a light press of the lips or a soft contact
in snooker and billiards, a slight contact between two balls

explanation.surface: Describes a delicate shot played on a snooker table.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue game played on a large table with coloured balls.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate press of the lips is a soft contact; in snooker the same word is a light touch of one ball on another.

clue.text: Bars over the river ready to close in times of emergency

definitions.text: Bars over the river ready to close in times of emergency

parts.words: Bars over the river ready to close in times of emergency
parts.note: barriers across a river that are shut when water levels threaten to overflow

explanation.surface: Pubs by the river are prepared to shut in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like pubs with closing times, but these are barriers across a river that shut against high water.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluices that control the flow of water and are shut to hold back a surge.

clue.text: Regular serviceman or woman

parts.note: a person regularly attending religious services, not a soldier in the regular army

explanation.surface: Describes a professional soldier of either sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular serviceman' suggests the armed forces; the service here is a religious one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who attends worship services at a place of worship regularly.

clue.text: Accommodation for workers on a stock-farm, nothing more

indicators.note: the extra word tells us the circle comes in addition, tacked onto the end of the farm

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm for raising cattle or other stock
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Housing on a cattle farm with no extra luxuries.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American West, a hut or group of huts housing ranch hands.

clue.text: Going straight down the fairway

definitions.meaning: heading in the right direction, keeping to plan
on a golf hole, a ball on the fairway is on the line of play

explanation.surface: A golfer's drive heads directly along the fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping to the intended route or plan; also literally being on the golf links' line of play.

clue.text: One getting on in a South African province, being born there

indicators.note: the pair of pieces is placed within the province's name

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thriving in South Africa because they were born there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins the pieces; NATAL is opened to hold I and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a country, especially one by birth, rather than a foreigner.

clue.text: Single' Oscar displayed in the Spanish palace

indicators.note: shown off in a new arrangement, the letters are set out differently

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, a single
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A lone Academy Award statuette is exhibited in a palace in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges I, OSCAR and EL. The answer is the vast royal palace and monastery north-west of Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sixteenth-century royal residence and monastery built by Philip II near Madrid.

clue.text: Invest in apparel

parts.note: en is French for in
a robe is a garment, a piece of apparel

explanation.surface: An instruction to put money into clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' looks financial; it is the old sense of clothing someone in robes of office.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest in the old sense is to clothe someone formally, dressing them in a gown.

clue.text: Indemnify small firm troubled Peru

indicators.note: disturbed and stirred up, the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Co is the short form of company, a firm

explanation.surface: Compensating a small company for trouble in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate someone for a loss or make good their expenses.

clue.text: Constellation appearing greyish-blue to us

parts.note: perse is an old word for a dark greyish-blue colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star group looks a dull blue to observers.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern star group named after the Greek hero who slew Medusa.

clue.text: Irritating beetle?

definitions.meaning: something that rubs and irritates is one that chafes
a large beetle, such as the cockchafer

explanation.surface: Asks whether an annoying insect is a beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: One that rubs sore is a word for an irritant; the same word names a family of large beetles.

clue.text: Tossing about in the small hours? Through gin, perhaps

definitions.text: Tossing about in the small hours?

indicators.note: a doubtful word showing the letters may be put another way

explanation.surface: Restless in bed in the early morning after too much gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepless spell of tossing and turning in bed after dark.

clue.text: Domestic worker of 20 with iron deficiency

indicators.note: something lacking, so the iron is missing from the other answer

parts.note: the answer to 20 down, the beetle
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A cleaner from 20 who is short of iron in the diet.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' refers to the answer of 20 down. A char is a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a woman paid to clean a house, short for charwoman.

clue.text: Member of the Liberal Party goes about Maidenhead

indicators.note: goes around the outside of the head letter, surrounding it

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal Party
the head of maiden is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Liberal Party member travels around the Berkshire town of Maidenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town in Berkshire, west of London, but here it gives M, the head of 'maiden'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body.

clue.text: It's. played, to benefit, about a couple of seconds

indicators.note: the benefit word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
two S's, S being the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Something is performed to good effect within a few seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument with a double reed, something a musician plays.

clue.text: Could be frail and easily broken

indicators.note: suggesting what the letters might become when rearranged

explanation.surface: Something might be delicate and liable to break.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbly and readily reduced to powder or fragments.

clue.text: They say it with flowers

parts.note: the florists' slogan 'say it with flowers', for wreaths sent as a message of sympathy

explanation.surface: People expressing their feelings with a bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreaths and bunches sent to a funeral as a mark of respect.
